# Proofreading comments and annotations {short-title="Annotations"}

## Collaborative comments {#sec-comments}

### Configuration in `_quarto.yml`

The `quarto-comments` extension (folder `_extensions/comments/`) is configured in
`_quarto.yml`, via the `quarto-comments:` key placed under the `extensions:` block {{< todo "You will need to walk me through your various YAML files at our next progress meeting." author="ag" >}}:

````yaml
extensions:
  quarto-comments:
    enabled: true
    authors:
      eb:
        name: "Eric Bavu"
      ag:
        name: "Abbé Grégoire"
      # Colors auto-assigned from Bootstrap 5 palette; override if needed:
      # nc:
      #   name: "Nicolas Conté"
      #   color_html: "#198754"
      #   color_latex: "green!30"
````

{{< pagebreak >}}


### The four comment types

````markdown
{{</* comment "Rephrase this sentence, it is too long." author="ag" */>}}
{{</* todo "Add a figure illustrating this point." author="eb" */>}}
{{</* note "See also Bringhurst 2004, §2.4." author="ag" */>}}
{{</* question "Is this result reproducible on another dataset?" author="ag" inline=true */>}}
````

**Rendered in context:**

Here is a sentence with a comment from the thesis supervisor (who added it directly in the {{< comment "This is a comment, to show that I too — Abbé Grégoire — am perfectly capable of editing a Quarto Markdown file myself!" author="ag" >}} `.qmd` file, because he is not shy about it!).

These comments are visible **only** if the `quarto-comments` option is set to `enabled: true` {{< todo "Remember to set this option to `false` before submitting to the reviewers!" author="eb" >}} in the `yaml` file — which is the case for this documentation.


It is also possible to add "long" inline comments {{< note "See Knuth 1984, chapter 12 — it would really be worth adding a discussion of this work here to show off all your knowledge of the existing literature, young apprentice." author="ag" inline=true >}} without taking up any space in the document margin. Useful to flesh out the text and add whole paragraphs. Note that, visually, the "inline" comment automatically breaks onto its own line and separates from the text in the PDF version, even when inserted mid-sentence.

::: {.callout-note}
## `inline=true` occupies the full line in PDF

In HTML, `inline=true` annotations appear as a compact coloured span, exactly
as wide as their content. In PDF, the `todonotes` package renders `\todo[inline]`
as a full-width coloured block — this is a design constraint of the package that
cannot be worked around without losing the ability to wrap long annotations across
lines.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Recommended: enable `wide_margins` for proofreading

For margin notes (without `inline`), it is **recommended to enable**
`extensions.quarto-comments.wide_margins: true` in your proofreading profile. The paper
is then widened outward by a dedicated strip (width adjustable via `extra_margin`) where
annotations display comfortably, with a grey background that alternates by page parity
(outer side, binding preserved).

**Per-chapter scoping.** The widening and the grey strip appear only in the **chapters
that actually contain comments**: a chapter without annotations stays at standard A4,
with no grey strip. The template detects the relevant chapters automatically (by scanning
the book's source files), so the commented areas stand out in a proofreading PDF without
needlessly widening the whole document. Acceptable cosmetic side effect: at the boundary
between a wide chapter and an A4 chapter, a blank spacing page (`\cleardoublepage`) may
inherit the previous width — irrelevant for the final deposit, where comments are off and
every page is back to A4.

When `wide_margins: false` (the default), the paper stays at standard A4 size: notes are
placed in the 2 cm outer margin. They therefore stay **narrow** (~1.5 cm) and long text
wraps over several lines. The **content** layout (text block) is strictly identical whether
`wide_margins` is `true` or `false`, and whether comments are enabled or not — only the
margin annotation zone changes.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Disable comments before final submission

Before submitting the thesis to the doctoral school and depositing it on theses.fr,
set `extensions.quarto-comments.enabled: false` in `_quarto.yml`. Annotations must not appear in the
official archived version.
:::

## Web annotations with Hypothesis (opt-in)

For remote proofreading, the HTML output can be enhanced with web annotations via
[Hypothesis](https://hypothes.is). Supervisors and reviewers select text in the browser
and add comments without touching the source files. Annotations are stored on Hypothesis
servers and tied to the page URL — they persist across renders as long as the URL stays
stable (GitHub Pages deployment recommended).

To enable, uncomment the following block in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
format:
  cnam-thesis-html:
    comments:
      hypothesis:
        theme: clean   # clean = discreet ; classic = sidebar always visible
```

Then create a private group on [hypothes.is](https://hypothes.is) and share the invite
link with your reviewers. Hypothesis is disabled by default in all profiles.
